t: Signature Apache TVM: What Apache TVM Is: A Compiler for ML Models
title: Signature Apache TVM: What Apache TVM Is: A Compiler for ML Models
description: The Signature counterpart is the SigForge compiler, Manon's original ML-to-machine-code design. SigForge mirrors the import-optimize-tune-lower pipeline but adds a determinism contract: the same model plus the same target description must produce bit-identical binaries on any build host. Every SigForge build emits a provenance record naming the model hash, the tuning log, and the backend version.
key_facts: ML models compiled like C source
Relay IR with fusion and layout passes

t: Signature Apache TVM: Relay IR: The Heart of the Compiler
title: Signature Apache TVM: Relay IR: The Heart of the Compiler
description: SigForge's IR is called the Loom: a typed tensor IR with explicit memory regions, so buffer lifetimes are visible to the optimizer instead of inferred. The Signature design requires every Loom pass to be invertible-logged — the compiler records which pass rewrote which node, and the log ships with the binary for audit.

t: Signature Apache TVM: Importing Models: ONNX, PyTorch, TensorFlow
title: Signature Apache TVM: Importing Models: ONNX, PyTorch, TensorFlow
description: SigForge's importer is called the intake, and it is deliberately strict: unknown operators are rejected with a named diagnostic instead of silently degraded. The Signature design pairs every intake with a coverage manifest listing which ops the target backend implements, so unsupported models fail fast at import time rather than mid-deployment.
key_facts: Strict op coverage prevents silent degradation

t: Signature Apache TVM: AutoTVM and Ansor: Letting the Machine Tune
title: Signature Apache TVM: AutoTVM and Ansor: Letting the Machine Tune
description: SigForge's tuner is the metronome: it searches schedules under a fixed trial budget and records the full search trace. The Signature twist is reproducibility — the metronome's random search is seeded, so re-tuning with the same seed and budget reproduces the same schedule, and the trace is checksummed into the build provenance.
key_facts: AutoTVM: template search; Ansor: from-scratch search
Tune on the real device via RPC
Logs reusable until model or silicon changes

t: Signature Apache TVM: Code Generation: From Relay to Machine Code
title: Signature Apache TVM: Code Generation: From Relay to Machine Code
description: SigForge lowers the Loom through a single machine IR with one backend per target family, and every backend is required to publish its calling convention and register discipline in a machine-readable target file. The Signature design makes the target file part of the audit trail — you cannot reproduce a binary without the exact target description that built it.

t: Signature Apache TVM: microTVM: ML on Bare Metal
title: Signature Apache TVM: microTVM: ML on Bare Metal
description: The Foundry-family micro backend in SigForge is called the spark: it emits MISRA-flavored C with bounded loops and no dynamic allocation. The Signature design adds a stack-proof certificate — the spark computes the worst-case stack depth of the generated kernels and refuses to emit code that could overflow the declared stack.
key_facts: No-OS runtime with static memory planning
One pipeline from GPU to Cortex-M
Worst-case stack proof for generated kernels

t: Signature Apache TVM: Quantization in the TVM Pipeline
title: Signature Apache TVM: Quantization in the TVM Pipeline
description: SigForge treats quantization as a contract stage: the press pass converts float to int8 with per-channel scales, then runs a differential test against the float model on a calibration set and reports per-layer error. The Signature design fails the build if any layer's error exceeds the manifest's stated tolerance — accuracy budgets are enforced by the compiler, not by hope.

t: Signature Apache TVM: Defensive Uses: Sovereign Model Deployment
title: Signature Apache TVM: Defensive Uses: Sovereign Model Deployment
description: SigForge was designed assurance-first: the provenance record is a first-class build product, the tuning trace is checksummed, and the target file is versioned. The Signature deployment ritual is 'replay the build' — an independent machine re-runs the recorded pipeline and must produce the identical binary before the artifact is cleared for fielding.
key_facts: Train anywhere, compile for locked-down targets
No framework or network at deploy time

t: Signature Apache TVM: BYOC: Bring Your Own Codegen
title: Signature Apache TVM: BYOC: Bring Your Own Codegen
description: SigForge's equivalent is the anvil interface: a backend registers its supported op patterns and its lowering callback, and the partitioner guarantees no supported pattern is left unclaimed. The Signature design requires anvil backends to declare their numerical behavior (rounding, saturation) in the target file, so mixed CPU/accelerator execution stays bit-predictable.

t: Signature Apache TVM: Debugging: Relay Inspection and Profiling
title: Signature Apache TVM: Debugging: Relay Inspection and Profiling
description: SigForge's inspector dumps the Loom after every pass with node-level provenance, and its differential runner compares stage outputs against the float reference automatically. The Signature design turns the most common bugs into build errors: layout mismatches at backend boundaries are rejected by the type checker before codegen ever runs.

t: Signature Apache TVM: Tuning at Scale: Board Farms and RPC
title: Signature Apache TVM: Tuning at Scale: Board Farms and RPC
description: The Foundry-family metronome scales the same way over what the Signature design calls a proving rack: a locked cabinet of target boards, each with a measured thermal profile, since hot silicon lies about timing. Every trial records board ID, temperature, and clock settings alongside the timing, and trials that drift thermally are discarded automatically.

t: Signature Apache TVM: Deployment Runtimes: Graph Executor and VM
title: Signature Apache TVM: Deployment Runtimes: Graph Executor and VM
description: SigForge's runtime is called the hearth: a single C runtime with a static-graph fast path and an explicit dynamic mode, selected at build time. The Signature design forbids silent mode switching — the binary's manifest states which mode it was built for, and the hearth asserts the mode at startup.

t: Signature Apache TVM: Testing: Correctness Before Speed
title: Signature Apache TVM: Testing: Correctness Before Speed
description: SigForge makes differential testing a compiler phase, not a CI afterthought: the press and every backend lowering must pass the reference comparison before the binary is emitted. The Signature design stores the acceptance set's hash in the build provenance, so anyone can verify exactly what 'correct' meant for a given artifact.
